objective: A newly produced fine-tune objectively better than stock Parakeet v3 for multilingual and multi-accent ASR
historical_note: The stage-3 update failed a different comparison against stage-2 EMA. That decision remains recorded. This study explicitly compares new fine-tuned artifacts with the stock model, as requested by the active goal.

candidate_family.method: Linear parameter interpolation between stock weights and the completed 800-step new fine-tune

development.multilingual_sets: The frozen 24 CV and 25 FLEURS development selection manifests from the first continuation
development.primary: 0.5 * CV language-macro WER + 0.5 * FLEURS language-macro WER
development.selection: Among eligible candidates, choose lowest primary development WER; ties choose the smaller fine-tuned fraction. If none qualifies, continue development without opening confirmation.

confirmation.exposure: Exclude training, historically inspected tests/validation, all first-run selection and confirmation, and this study's development utterances. CV additionally excludes previously exposed speakers globally. FLEURS excludes within-language sentence identities; speaker identity is unavailable. No claim of upstream pretraining decontamination.
confirmation.coverage_requirement: At least 20 primary languages, each with at least 20 distinct source-qualified resampling groups across its included corpora. Report every remaining available language descriptively. All 25 trained languages retain their development regression checks.
confirmation.primary: Equal-weight macro WER over eligible languages. Within a language, pool reference-word and error counts from CV, FLEURS, VoxPopuli, FTSpeech and RixVox confirmation manifests. Include a source-language stratum in the primary only with at least 5 groups; require at least 20 distinct groups across the language. English accent, learner, dialect and LibriSpeech auxiliary sets do not alter the multilingual primary.
confirmation.english_requirements: Fresh CV English/accent speakers plus previously unused source-held-out learner/dialect audio where available, and LibriSpeech test-clean. No confirmation corpus may regress by more than 0.3 WER percentage points; paired 95% upper bounds must also be below the 0.3-point noninferiority margin for the English aggregate and each core/learner/dialect corpus with adequate groups.
confirmation.bootstrap_unit: Global source-qualified speaker ID; FLEURS parallel sentence ID when speaker is unavailable, shared across language strata
confirmation.repeat_policy: Open confirmation only after a candidate is selected. A failed confirmation is consumed and cannot be reused as a fresh gate for another candidate.
confirmation.interpretation: Establish average multilingual superiority and English noninferiority on the defined suite; disclose all measured per-language and accent tradeoffs, coverage gaps and public pretraining limitations. Do not claim universal superiority.
confirmation.additional_source_note: New sources are confirmation only. VoxPopuli uses published test, gold transcripts and source speaker IDs. FTSpeech uses official test-balanced and test-other. RixVox uses previously unused official dev+test to include 29 source speakers; human parliamentary protocols are automatically aligned and not always verbatim. English Dialects speaker IDs are configuration-qualified because bare numeric IDs collide. Source-held-out English requires disjoint source speakers and recordings; repeated prompts and transcript-novel subsets are reported.
confirmation.family_metric: For each of CV, FLEURS, VoxPopuli, FTSpeech and RixVox, language-macro WER over strata with at least 5 groups. Every family must improve in point estimate; all family intervals and sample sizes are disclosed.
confirmation.english_metric: Equal weight to English corpus aggregates: Common Voice (main English plus separately reserved accent recordings), FLEURS English, VoxPopuli English, VoxPopuli accented English, LibriSpeech test-clean, SpeechOcean official test, and English Dialects source-speaker holdout. Noninferiority requires the aggregate paired 95% upper bound below +0.3 pp and separately the same bound for LibriSpeech, SpeechOcean and English Dialects. Every English corpus point regression must be <=0.3 pp. Individual accent slices are reported with uncertainty; no all-accent superiority claim.
confirmation.duration_policy: For newly converted HF sources, retain complete clips from 0.4 through 60 seconds. Existing frozen manifests and official LibriSpeech/SpeechOcean retain their original full clips. No truncation or prediction-based filtering.

artifact_requirements: No added inference model or routing dependency

amendment.reason: A prediction-free metadata audit found only 12 languages meeting the initial per-source CV/FLEURS group requirement. The benchmark is expanded with public parliamentary speech and the primary is made language-balanced across these sources. This is a changed estimand, prospectively declared, not a claim that the old coverage design was met.
changes: Language-level pooled within-language WER and macro aggregation
20 groups per primary language, with at least 5 groups per contributing source stratum
Explicit English corpus aggregation and retained 0.3 pp margins
unchanged: Paired 95% primary interval entirely below zero
Every multilingual source family must improve
Development selection rules and candidate family
Only one selected candidate opens this confirmation gate
